note: Food as missions rather than listings, the Paris shape. Each mission is a small assignment in a particular set of streets — candidates, what to order, how to judge, where to go afterwards. Moods map to missions in js/app.js.

items.title: An Italian Morning in North Beach
items.area: Four old Italian shops within five minutes of Washington Square
items.brief: North Beach was San Francisco's Little Italy, and a handful of the shops that fed it are still run by the same families. Start early — the focaccia sells out — and eat your way round Washington Square in the order below.
items.test: The focaccia should be soft and oily on the bottom, not bready; the cannoli shell should crack, which means it was filled after you ordered.

candidates.name: Liguria Bakery
candidates.order: A slab of plain or onion focaccia, wrapped in paper
candidates.note: Since 1911. Opens early, shuts when the trays are empty — often before noon.

candidates.name: Molinari Delicatessen
candidates.order: Take a number. A sandwich on a sweet roll for later
candidates.note: Since 1896; they cure their own salami.

candidates.name: Victoria Pastry Company
candidates.order: A cannoli, filled to order
candidates.note: Or Stella Pastry on Columbus for the sacripantina.

candidates.name: Caffe Trieste
candidates.order: A cappuccino, at a table
candidates.note: The first espresso house on the West Coast, 1956.

then.text: Eat the sandwich on the grass in Washington Square
Browse City Lights Books on Columbus

items.why: The quickest way to understand what North Beach was, and it still tastes of it. Four shops, a park and a coffee, and nothing on the list is newer than 1956.
items.hoursNote: A morning, Tuesday to Saturday — Liguria is closed Sundays and Mondays and can sell out before noon.

items.title: Chinatown, One Bite at a Time
items.area: Stockton Street and Grant Avenue, a ten-minute loop
items.priceNote: ~$25 for two — most things are a few dollars
items.brief: The oldest Chinatown in North America is at its best in the morning, when Stockton Street is doing its shopping. Eat standing up, a few dollars at a time, and finish sitting down with tea.
items.test: A good egg tart is still warm and barely set in the middle. Good dim sum to go is steamed that morning and the wrapper is thin enough to see through.

candidates.name: Golden Gate Bakery
candidates.order: Two egg tarts, warm
candidates.note: Closes without warning for weeks at a time. If there is a queue, join it.

candidates.name: Good Mong Kok Bakery
candidates.order: Har gow, siu mai and a char siu bao, to take away
candidates.note: Cash, a queue out the door, priced by the piece.

candidates.name: Red Blossom Tea Company
candidates.order: Ask them to brew an oolong tasting
candidates.note: A family tea shop on Grant since 1985.

then.text: Walk up Grant Avenue to the Dragon Gate
Sit in Portsmouth Square with the old men playing cards

items.why: Chinatown rewards the person who eats small and keeps walking. This is the cheapest good morning in San Francisco.
items.hoursNote: Best in the morning, when Stockton Street is shopping.

items.title: Settle the Burrito Argument
items.area: Three taquerias on Mission Street, within a ten-minute walk
items.brief: The Mission burrito is San Francisco's own dish, and everyone who lives here has a side. Share one burrito at each of three places — the same filling everywhere, carne asada — and decide which side you are on.
items.test: Judge the tortilla (steamed or crisped on the plancha?), the meat (charred at the edges?), and whether it holds together to the last bite. Rice is the argument.

candidates.name: La Taqueria
candidates.order: Carne asada burrito, 'dorado' style — no rice
candidates.note: The purist. No rice, crisped tortilla, a queue at lunch.

candidates.name: Taqueria El Farolito
candidates.order: Super carne asada burrito
candidates.note: The heavyweight. Open very late, and enormous.

candidates.name: Taqueria Cancún
candidates.order: Super burrito, the one with avocado
candidates.note: The comfortable one, with a salsa bar.

then.text: Walk it off to Bi-Rite Creamery, then Dolores Park
Balmy Alley murals, five minutes from La Taqueria

items.why: You will not agree with anyone afterwards, but you will know why they think what they think.
items.hoursNote: Lunch or dinner; all three open late morning.

items.title: Saturday at the Ferry Building
items.area: The farmers market around the Ferry Building, on the Embarcadero
items.priceNote: ~$50 for two, eating as you go
items.brief: On Saturday mornings the Ferry Plaza Farmers Market wraps round the Ferry Building and the best of Northern California comes to town. Go before ten, graze, buy one thing to cook, and eat lunch on the water.
items.test: Taste before you buy — every stall offers. Buy only what you could not get in a supermarket.

candidates.name: Ferry Plaza Farmers Market
candidates.step: Walk the stalls once before buying anything; stone fruit in summer, citrus in winter
candidates.note: Saturdays from 8. Also Tuesdays and Thursdays, smaller.

candidates.name: Blue Bottle Coffee, inside the Ferry Building
candidates.order: A New Orleans iced coffee

candidates.name: Hog Island Oyster Company
candidates.order: A dozen Sweetwaters at the bar
candidates.note: Queue before it opens, or eat at the counter outside.

then.text: Walk the Embarcadero north towards Pier 39 and the sea lions
Take the F-line streetcar back along the water

items.why: San Francisco is a food city because of what grows within a hundred miles of it. This is where you see that.

items.title: The Palo Alto Croissant Test
items.area: Three bakeries between Lytton Avenue and Town & Country
items.brief: Palo Alto has quietly got very good at laminated dough. Buy one plain croissant at each — plain, or the test means nothing — and eat them within the hour.
items.test: Does it shatter when torn, is the inside honeycombed rather than bready, and does it taste of butter after you swallow?

candidates.name: Mademoiselle Colette
candidates.order: Plain croissant, then the almond one
candidates.note: The French one, on Lytton.

candidates.name: Manresa Bread
candidates.order: Plain croissant, and a loaf for later
candidates.note: From the team behind the Michelin-starred Manresa.

candidates.name: La Baguette
candidates.order: Plain croissant
candidates.note: The one in the Stanford Shopping Center.

then.text: Reset with a coffee at Coupa Café on Ramona
Eat the winner in the Rodin Sculpture Garden at Stanford

items.why: The same hour you would spend in Paris, and you will come out knowing which bakery is yours.
items.hoursNote: A morning — bakeries run low on croissants by midday.

items.title: Three Scoops on University
items.area: University Avenue and the Stanford Shopping Center, an evening walk
items.brief: Palo Alto takes its ice cream seriously and the good ones are a short walk apart. One small scoop at each, the same flavour family everywhere — something with caramel or pistachio — and a walk in between.
items.test: Judge on texture first (dense and elastic, or light and icy?), then whether the flavour tastes of the thing rather than of sugar.

candidates.name: Scoop Microcreamery
candidates.order: One small scoop, their seasonal flavour

candidates.name: Bacio di Latte
candidates.order: Pistachio gelato
candidates.note: At the Stanford Shopping Center, a pleasant walk along El Camino.

candidates.name: The Penny Ice Creamery
candidates.order: Anything with the torched marshmallow
candidates.note: In Town & Country, across El Camino.

then.text: Walk back down University after dark, when the trees are lit

items.why: An evening walk with a reason to it — and a genuinely different ice cream at each stop.

items.title: Noodles on Castro Street
items.area: Castro Street, Mountain View — all within two blocks
items.brief: Castro Street is one of the best noodle streets on the Peninsula. Share a bowl at each place across an evening — handmade Japanese udon, then northern Chinese hand-cut noodles and dumplings.
items.test: The noodle is the whole test: bounce and bite, whether it holds the sauce, and whether it was made in the building.

candidates.name: Udon Mugizo
candidates.order: Mentaiko cream udon, or kake udon with tempura
candidates.note: Handmade udon. Queue at lunch.

candidates.name: Seasons Noodle & Dumpling Garden
candidates.order: Hand-cut noodles and a plate of dumplings

then.text: Finish at Red Rock Coffee at the top of Castro
Caltrain is at the bottom of the street

items.why: The most convincing evidence that the best food in Silicon Valley is on its main streets, not its campuses.
items.hoursNote: An evening; Udon Mugizo has the longest queue at lunch.

items.title: Sunday Market, Castro Street Pastry
items.area: The Caltrain station lot and the top of Castro Street
items.brief: On Sunday mornings the Mountain View farmers market fills the Caltrain lot. Walk it first, buy fruit and something hot, then take it up Castro Street for coffee and pastry.
items.test: At the market: buy what is at the peak of its season and nothing else. At Maison Alyzée: the plain croissant decides it.

candidates.name: Mountain View Farmer's Market
candidates.step: One lap before you buy. Hot food at the far end.
candidates.note: Sundays, mornings only.

candidates.name: Maison Alyzée
candidates.order: Croissant and a kouign-amann

candidates.name: Dana Street Roasting Company
candidates.order: A house espresso, and a bag of beans for the week

then.text: Pioneer Park, behind the library, for a picnic

items.why: A proper Sunday morning without leaving the South Bay.
items.hoursNote: Sunday morning — the market packs up around 1.

items.title: Dumplings, Then Dessert, at Santana Row
items.area: Valley Fair and Santana Row, facing each other across Stevens Creek
items.brief: Put your name down at Din Tai Fung in Valley Fair, wander Santana Row across the road while you wait, eat dumplings, then walk the Row for dessert — one thing each, shared.
items.test: Xiao long bao: lift it by the knot without tearing it, and the soup should be hot and clear. Dessert: pick the one you cannot get anywhere else in the South Bay.

candidates.name: Din Tai Fung
candidates.order: Pork xiao long bao, spicy wontons, the green beans
candidates.note: Join the waitlist online before you arrive.

candidates.name: Smitten Ice Cream
candidates.order: Salted caramel, churned to order

candidates.name: Lady M
candidates.order: A slice of green tea mille crêpes
candidates.note: Back in Valley Fair, near Din Tai Fung.

candidates.name: SomiSomi
candidates.order: Ube soft serve in a taiyaki cone
candidates.note: The alternative to Lady M.

then.text: Sit by the fire pits in the middle of the Row

items.why: A night out that is easy to plan and hard to get wrong.
items.hoursNote: An evening; the Din Tai Fung queue is shortest before 6.

items.title: An Evening on Broadway
items.area: Three stops along Broadway, downtown Redwood City, within a ten-minute walk
items.brief: Downtown Redwood City does a good evening on one street. Start with a beer and a pretzel in a German beer garden, walk down Broadway to wood-fired pizza, and finish with a scoop of odd ice cream a few doors on.
items.test: The pizza decides it: a blistered, chewy crust that still holds its shape in the middle. The ice cream should taste of what the name says, however strange that is.

candidates.name: Gourmet Haus Staudt
candidates.order: A German beer on tap and a soft pretzel with mustard
candidates.note: The beer garden is out the back; the German grocery at the front is worth a look.

candidates.name: Vesta
candidates.order: One pizza from the wood oven and a small plate to share
candidates.note: Busy at dinner. Closed Sundays.

candidates.name: Humphry Slocombe
candidates.order: Secret Breakfast — bourbon and cornflakes

then.text: Sit on the steps of Courthouse Square with the ice cream
Or a late cocktail at LV Mar, next door to Vesta

items.why: A proper night out without driving anywhere. Three good places, one street, and each stop sets up the next.
items.hoursNote: Tuesday to Saturday evening. Vesta is closed Sundays, and the beer garden closes at 8 on Mondays.

items.title: A Taiwanese Sunday in Cupertino
items.area: Stevens Creek Boulevard, from Liang’s Village to De Anza College
items.brief: Cupertino is one of the best places outside Taiwan to eat like you are in Taipei. Start with a Taiwanese breakfast, walk the Sunday farmers market at De Anza College, then finish with a properly brewed tea.
items.test: Breakfast: the fried cruller should be crisp, and the soy milk made in-house. Tea: order the oolong without much sugar, so you can taste whether it was brewed to order.

candidates.name: Liang’s Village
candidates.order: Taiwanese breakfast: warm soy milk, a fried cruller, a scallion pancake
candidates.note: Breakfast is Friday to Sunday from 8. Beef noodle soup is on from 11.

candidates.name: De Anza College Farmers’ Market
candidates.step: One lap first, then Asian greens and whatever fruit is in season
candidates.note: Sundays 9 to 1.

candidates.name: Chicha San Chen
candidates.order: An oolong or Dong Ding milk tea, low sugar
candidates.note: Opens at 11:30. Expect a queue.

then.text: Take a dozen from Donut Wheel home — it never closes
Or a proper espresso at Voyager Craft Coffee

items.why: A morning that shows what Cupertino is really good at, and costs very little.
items.hoursNote: Sunday morning only: breakfast from 8, the market 9 to 1, tea from 11:30.
